newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end down, TELCO falls before results.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end down, TELCO falls before results.

text.p: Bombay blue chips closed broadly lower on Monday after an early rally attracted profit-booking, traders said.
Market action was focussed on truckmaker TELCO ahead of its 1996/97 (April-March) results due late evening, they said.
"There isn't any great action in the market," said Rakesh Chandak, dealer at Lloyds Securities. "We saw some liquidation of long positions build up in TELCO."
Shares of TELCO dropped to 389.50, but ended with a net loss of 7.0 rupees at 393.0 after profit-booking wiped out early gains, traders said.
Analysts polled on Monday ahead of TELCO's 1996/97 results forecast an average net profit of 7.20 billion rupees, up 36 percent from 5.3 billion in the previous year.
Most analysts raised their net forecasts for TELCO after sharply improved March sales figures were released last month.
TELCO sold 29,190 units in March, up from 22,283 vehicles in the same month of 1996. The company sold an average 16,900 vehicles in the first eleven months of 1996/97.
Analysts had pegged March sales at around 22,000 units as vehicle sales generally pick up during the last month of the fiscal year when buyers take advantage of depreciation benefits.
Shares of Hero Honda gained 0.75 rupees to 491.50 ahead of its 196/97 results due on Tuesday. Over 62,800 shares were traded at the Bombay exchange.

The stock has surged 50 percent in the last one month on market expectations of the company announcing a bonus share issue. Heavy buying by foreign funds has aided the price surge, market sources said.
The National Stock Exchange 50-stock index climbed 1.30 points to close at 1,028.20
